```{r Frodo, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(performance)
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)   
library(mgcv)
library(emmeans)
library(DHARMa)
library(vcd)
library(broom)
library(broom.mixed)
library(caret)
library(ggfortify)
library(effects)
library(factoextra)
library(gridExtra)
library(corrplot)
library(kableExtra)
library(gratia)
library(lme4)
library(ggrepel)
df_list <- list()
probs <- read.csv("C:/Users/Thomsen.Bolton/Downloads/birdsimr/Terr/probs.csv", header = TRUE)
for (i in 1:52) {
  df<- read.csv(paste0("C:/Users/Thomsen.Bolton/Downloads/birdsimr/Terr/sim_", i, ".csv"), header = TRUE)
  df <- filter(df, Sex == "F")
  df$birdID=factor(df$birdID)
  df$Sex=factor(df$Sex)
  df$Terrs=factor(df$Terrs)
  df$fac.yr=factor(df$Yr)
  # Calculate z-scores within each year
  df <- df %>%
  group_by(fac.yr) %>%
  mutate(
    z_score = (Fledge - mean(Fledge, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(Fledge, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
  df$Eggs <- ifelse(df$Fledge > 0, 1, 0)
  
  df_list[[i]] <- df
}
delta_aic_pois <- matrix(rep(0, 52 * 3), nrow = 52, ncol = 3)
colnames(delta_aic_pois) <- c("BandID", "Terr", "BandID+Terr")
delta_aic_binom <- matrix(rep(0, 52 * 3), nrow = 52, ncol = 3)
colnames(delta_aic_binom) <- c("BandID", "Terr", "BandID+Terr")
# Doing this just to see how many terr only models best optimize BIC. 
delta_bic_pois <- matrix(rep(0, 52 * 3), nrow = 52, ncol = 3)
colnames(delta_bic_pois) <- c("BandID", "Terr", "BandID+Terr")
delta_bic_binom <- matrix(rep(0, 52 * 3), nrow = 52, ncol = 3)
colnames(delta_bic_binom) <- c("BandID", "Terr", "BandID+Terr")
```

For this report, we generated 50 different simulated data sets varying probability of mate fidelity, a pair's territory fidelity, a single male's territory fidelity, and a single female's territory fidelity. Latin hyper cube sampling (LHS) was used to generate these probabilities for the 50 different runs. In addition to to the 50 runs generated from the LHS, we also generated two simulated data sets, where probabilities were chosen to either show the territory effect, or to make the territory effect more difficult to detect. 

I am using GLMMs instead of GAMMs. The reason being for this is that we did try modelling year with both cyclic and cubic regression splines. However, edfs on the year smoother were large and the k-indices were often too small, meaning our basis dimension was inadequate. Since we only have 20 years in the data set, we cannot get the adequate dimension for our basis. 

In addition to computing AIC and BIC for models, we also compute Cohen's Kappa for the binomial models and marginal and conditional $R^2$ for the Poisson models. 

This report does not include models fit with a z-score response. All models seemed to violate assumptions. 

The probability of fledgling were randomly drawn from a beta(14, (14/0.65 - 14)) distribution for good territories, a beta(9, (9/0.55 - 9)) distribution for mediocre territories, and a beta(14, (5/0.45 - 5)) distribution for bad territories. Note that maybe playing with priors could be interesting. I initially ran the simulation where priors were very different and the models seemed to have an easier time picking up on the territory effect.

# Simulation 1 

## Number of fledgling as the response (Poisson)

```{r , comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}

form.list <- list(
  Fledge ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID),

  Fledge ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | Terrs),

  Fledge ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID) + (1 | Terrs)
)

pois.summary.results <- list()
pois.random.results  <- list()
pois.fixed.results   <- list()

models <- list()

for(i in seq_along(form.list)){

  mod <- glmer(
    form.list[[i]],
    data = df_list[[1]],
    family = poisson
  )

  models[[i]] <- mod
  r2 = r2_nakagawa(mod)

  pois.summary.results[[i]] <-
    glance(mod) %>%
    add_column(condtional_R2 = r2$R2_conditional,
               marginal_R2 = r2$R2_marginal,
      Family = "Poisson",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  pois.random.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "ran_pars") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Poisson",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  pois.fixed.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "fixed") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Poisson",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )
}

pois.summary.tbl <- bind_rows(pois.summary.results) %>% arrange(AIC)
pois.random.tbl  <- bind_rows(pois.random.results)
pois.fixed.tbl   <- bind_rows(pois.fixed.results)

kable(pois.summary.tbl)
kable(pois.random.tbl)
kable(pois.fixed.tbl)

aic_vec <- c(pois.summary.results[[1]]$AIC, pois.summary.results[[2]]$AIC, 
             pois.summary.results[[3]]$AIC)
delta_aic <- aic_vec - min(aic_vec)
delta_aic_pois[1, ] <- delta_aic
bic_vec <- c(pois.summary.results[[1]]$BIC, pois.summary.results[[2]]$BIC, 
             pois.summary.results[[3]]$BIC)
delta_bic <- bic_vec - min(bic_vec)
delta_bic_pois[1, ] <- delta_bic
```



```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[1]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[2]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[3]])
plot(sim)
```

The territory only model performed best on all model selection criteria. 

## Eggs (Binomial)

```{r , comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
form.list <- list(

  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID),

  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | Terrs),

  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID) + (1 | Terrs)

)

binom.summary.results <- list()
binom.random.results  <- list()
binom.fixed.results   <- list()

models <- list()

for(i in seq_along(form.list)){

  mod <- glmer(
    form.list[[i]],
    data = df_list[[1]],
    family = binomial
  )

  models[[i]] <- mod
  pred_prob <- predict(mod, type = "response")  # includes RE by default

  # Classify predictions into successes and failures
  pred_class <- ifelse(pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)
  obs_class <- df_list[[1]]$Eggs  
  
  # Build confusion matrix and compute kappa
  tab <- table(Predicted = pred_class, Observed = obs_class)

  binom.summary.results[[i]] <-
    glance(mod) %>%
    add_column(Kappa = round(Kappa(tab)$Unweighted[1], 3),
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  binom.random.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "ran_pars") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  binom.fixed.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "fixed") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )
}

binom.summary.tbl <- bind_rows(binom.summary.results) %>% arrange(AIC)
binom.random.tbl  <- bind_rows(binom.random.results)
binom.fixed.tbl   <- bind_rows(binom.fixed.results)

kable(binom.summary.tbl)
kable(binom.random.tbl)
kable(binom.fixed.tbl)

aic_vec <- c(binom.summary.results[[1]]$AIC, binom.summary.results[[2]]$AIC, 
             binom.summary.results[[3]]$AIC)
delta_aic <- aic_vec - min(aic_vec)
delta_aic_binom[1, ] <- delta_aic
bic_vec <- c(binom.summary.results[[1]]$BIC, binom.summary.results[[2]]$BIC, 
             binom.summary.results[[3]]$BIC)
delta_bic <- bic_vec - min(bic_vec)
delta_bic_binom[1, ] <- delta_bic
```

The territory only model performed worst on model selection criteria

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[1]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[2]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[3]])
plot(sim)
```

A slight violation of model assumptions. 

## Probabilites used to generate simulation 1

```{r , comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
string <- cat(
  paste0(
    "Simulation 1\n",
    "Probability of mate fidelity: ", round(probs$pFidel[1], 3), "\n",
    "Probability of pair dispersal: ", round(probs$pDispP[1], 3), "\n",
    "Probability of single male dispersal: ", round(probs$pDispM[1], 3), "\n",
    "Probability of single female dispersal: ", round(probs$pDispF[1], 3)
  )
)
```

```{r , comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID) + (1 | Terrs)

)

binom.summary.results <- list()
binom.random.results  <- list()
binom.fixed.results   <- list()

models <- list()

for(i in seq_along(form.list)){

  mod <- glmer(
    form.list[[i]],
    data = df_list[[21]],
    family = binomial
  )

  models[[i]] <- mod
  pred_prob <- predict(mod, type = "response")  # includes RE by default

  # Classify predictions into successes and failures
  pred_class <- ifelse(pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)
  obs_class <- df_list[[21]]$Eggs  
  
  # Build confusion matrix and compute kappa
  tab <- table(Predicted = pred_class, Observed = obs_class)

  binom.summary.results[[i]] <-
    glance(mod) %>%
    add_column(Kappa = round(Kappa(tab)$Unweighted[1], 3),
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  binom.random.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "ran_pars") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  binom.fixed.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "fixed") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )
}

binom.summary.tbl <- bind_rows(binom.summary.results) %>% arrange(AIC)
binom.random.tbl  <- bind_rows(binom.random.results)
binom.fixed.tbl   <- bind_rows(binom.fixed.results)

kable(binom.summary.tbl)
kable(binom.random.tbl)
kable(binom.fixed.tbl)

aic_vec <- c(binom.summary.results[[1]]$AIC, binom.summary.results[[2]]$AIC, 
             binom.summary.results[[3]]$AIC)
delta_aic <- aic_vec - min(aic_vec)
delta_aic_binom[21, ] <- delta_aic
bic_vec <- c(binom.summary.results[[1]]$BIC, binom.summary.results[[2]]$BIC, 
             binom.summary.results[[3]]$BIC)
delta_bic <- bic_vec - min(bic_vec)
delta_bic_binom[21, ] <- delta_bic
```

Territory only model is performing best on AIC and BIC.

Territory only model is performing best on AIC and BIC. Note that we don't include $R^2$s because some variance components were too close to 0, leading to numerical instability. 

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[3]])

```

Similar to the previous batch of diagnostic plots for Poisson response.

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
  Fledge ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | Terrs),

  Fledge ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID) + (1 | Terrs)
)

pois.summary.results <- list()
pois.random.results  <- list()
pois.fixed.results   <- list()

models <- list()

for(i in seq_along(form.list)){

  mod <- glmer(
    form.list[[i]],
    data = df_list[[51]],
    family = poisson
  )

  models[[i]] <- mod
  r2 = r2_nakagawa(mod)

  pois.summary.results[[i]] <-
    glance(mod) %>%
    add_column(condtional_R2 = r2$R2_conditional,
               marginal_R2 = r2$R2_marginal,
      Family = "Poisson",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  pois.random.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "ran_pars") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Poisson",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  pois.fixed.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "fixed") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Poisson",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )
}

pois.summary.tbl <- bind_rows(pois.summary.results) %>% arrange(AIC)
pois.random.tbl  <- bind_rows(pois.random.results)
pois.fixed.tbl   <- bind_rows(pois.fixed.results)

kable(pois.summary.tbl)
kable(pois.random.tbl)
kable(pois.fixed.tbl)

aic_vec <- c(pois.summary.results[[1]]$AIC, pois.summary.results[[2]]$AIC, 
             pois.summary.results[[3]]$AIC)
delta_aic <- aic_vec - min(aic_vec)
delta_aic_pois[51, ] <- delta_aic
bic_vec <- c(pois.summary.results[[1]]$BIC, pois.summary.results[[2]]$BIC, 
             pois.summary.results[[3]]$BIC)
delta_bic <- bic_vec - min(bic_vec)
delta_bic_pois[51, ] <- delta_bic
```

Territory only model seems to be performing the best on all criteria

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[1]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[2]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[3]])
plot(sim)
```

Diagnostics look good. 

## Eggs (Binomial)

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE}
form.list <- list(

  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID),

  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | Terrs),

  Eggs ~ factor(fac.yr) + (1 | birdID) + (1 | Terrs)

)

binom.summary.results <- list()
binom.random.results  <- list()
binom.fixed.results   <- list()

models <- list()

for(i in seq_along(form.list)){

  mod <- glmer(
    form.list[[i]],
    data = df_list[[51]],
    family = binomial
  )

  models[[i]] <- mod
  pred_prob <- predict(mod, type = "response")  # includes RE by default

  # Classify predictions into successes and failures
  pred_class <- ifelse(pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)
  obs_class <- df_list[[51]]$Eggs  
  
  # Build confusion matrix and compute kappa
  tab <- table(Predicted = pred_class, Observed = obs_class)

  binom.summary.results[[i]] <-
    glance(mod) %>%
    add_column(Kappa = round(Kappa(tab)$Unweighted[1], 3),
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  binom.random.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "ran_pars") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )

  binom.fixed.results[[i]] <-
    tidy(mod, effects = "fixed") %>%
    add_column(
      Family = "Binomial",
      RE = c("BirdID","Terr","BirdID+Terr")[i]
    )
}

binom.summary.tbl <- bind_rows(binom.summary.results) %>% arrange(AIC)
binom.random.tbl  <- bind_rows(binom.random.results)
binom.fixed.tbl   <- bind_rows(binom.fixed.results)

kable(binom.summary.tbl)
kable(binom.random.tbl)
kable(binom.fixed.tbl)

aic_vec <- c(binom.summary.results[[1]]$AIC, binom.summary.results[[2]]$AIC, 
             binom.summary.results[[3]]$AIC)
delta_aic <- aic_vec - min(aic_vec)
delta_aic_binom[51, ] <- delta_aic
bic_vec <- c(binom.summary.results[[1]]$BIC, binom.summary.results[[2]]$BIC, 
             binom.summary.results[[3]]$BIC)
delta_bic <- bic_vec - min(bic_vec)
delta_bic_binom[51, ] <- delta_bic
```

Terr only does well on all but Kappa. 

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[1]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[2]])
plot(sim)
sim <- simulateResiduals(models[[3]])
plot(sim)
```

Terr only diagnostics look good.

# Detla AIC Plots 

Here, we explore the relationships between probabilities of dispersal, and mate fidelity, and delta AIC for each response variable and random effect structure.  

## Fledge Response

### Band ID 

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
ord <- order(probs$pFidel)
plot(probs$pFidel[ord], delta_aic_pois[ord,1], type = "b", 
xlab = "probability of mate fidelity",
ylab = expression(Delta*AIC))
abline(h = 2, col = "red", lty = "dashed")
ord <- order(probs$pDispP)
plot(probs$pDispP[ord], delta_aic_pois[ord,1], type = "b", 
xlab = "probability of pair dispersal",
ylab = expression(Delta*AIC))
abline(h = 2, col = "red", lty = "dashed")
ord <- order(probs$pDispM)
plot(probs$pDispM[ord], delta_aic_pois[ord,1], type = "b", 
xlab = "probability of male dispersal",
ylab = expression(Delta*AIC))
abline(h = 2, col = "red", lty = "dashed")
ord <- order(probs$pDispF)
plot(probs$pDispF[ord], delta_aic_pois[ord,1], type = "b", 
xlab = "probability of female dispersal",
ylab = expression(Delta*AIC))
abline(h = 2, col = "red", lty = "dashed")
```

There does seem to be some low $\Delta$ AICs when male dispersal is high, other than that, I don't see a terribly clear pattern in any of these plots.

# Heat maps

## Fledge response models 

### Band ID only models

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(terra)
library(fields)

# Example data frame
df <- data.frame(
  pFidel = probs$pFidel,
  pDispP = probs$pDispP,
  deltaAIC = delta_aic_pois[,1]
)
# Fit surface
fit <- Tps(cbind(df$pFidel, df$pDispP), df$deltaAIC)

# Prediction grid
grid <- expand.grid(
  x = seq(min(df$pFidel), max(df$pFidel), length = 200),
  y = seq(min(df$pDispP), max(df$pDispP), length = 200)
)

grid$z <- predict(fit, grid)

# Convert to raster
r <- rast(grid, type = "xyz")

plot(r, xlab = "Probability of mate fidelity", ylab = "Probability of pair dispersal")
points(df$pFidel, df$pDispP, pch = 16, cex = 0.3)
```

```{r, comment = NA, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
points(df$x, df$y, pch = 16, cex = 0.3)
```

It seems that female dispersal is leading this relation and I feel that it makes sense that as females disperse more, that we can more easier detect the territory effect, i.e., $\Delta$ AIC gets higher. Note that $\Delta$ AIC is still quite low. 

# Some Summaries 
0.
From the summary plots and table, it seems that the Poisson models do a better job detecting the territory effect that was coded in the simulation, and the models that fit both random effects seems to still do well on model selection criteria. There seemed to be some slight patterns in $\Delta$ AIC based on certain simulation probabilistic settings, but surprisingly nothing super clear.
